story: At 3:17 on a rainy Tuesday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at his workbench in his house, determined to finish the LED rope light circuit on his golf cart. Out on Magnolia Loop, Donna is cheerfully announcing that she and Gary are entering the doubles ladder, then asks Hal to tip her off about the good court times, while Hal grumbles that her flamingos break the three-ornament rule. Over at the Rec Center, Rosa is studying the ladder standings board, determined to figure out when Donna usually plays.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Pick the cart wiring back up and finish the LED rope light circuit
Rosa (ladder standings board): Check the standings and sign-up times to see when Donna usually plays

gary.thought_process: Donna headed out to book the court for tomorrow morning, and I'm alone in the house with the afternoon ahead. The cart wiring is still unfinished and I promised her the lights would be sorted by then. The soldering iron is out of the way, but I can't ride around with half-finished rope light. The workbench is where the wiring lives, so that's where I should be. Nobody's around to talk to, and the guilt about the speaker and the permits can wait; the parade is the real goal. Get the circuit done properly, keep it unamplified until I sort out the paperwork, and keep my word to Donna.

parameters.content: Pick the cart wiring back up and finish the LED rope light circuit

donna.thought_process: I just got to Magnolia Loop with the spare paddle and iced tea in the cart. Gary said he'd book it for tomorrow and bring sneakers, and he's finishing up at his workbench, so I shouldn't pester him again. Hal is right here, and Hal knows everything that happens on this street, so I might as well spread the word about the pickleball ladder and see if he's got any gossip. Then I can book the court time at the rec center.

parameters.content: Hal, you're just the man I wanted. Gary and I are entering the doubles ladder, so don't be surprised when we start climbing. And if you hear anything about who's got the good court times, you come tell me first.

hal.thought_process: Donna just arrived on Magnolia Loop, right by her flamingo flock, and I already counted them at Tick 16 and read the bulletin board at Tick 17. I've been keeping score on my neighbors for hours now, and Rosa's dinner note has me wondering if I'm more rulebook than friend. But the limit is three ornaments visible from the street (L-02), and my count didn't come out to three. Better to say it to her face, gruffly but fairly, than log it behind her back first. I'll mention the count and the rule, then leave her room to fix it before I take anything to the committee.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Donna. I counted your flamingos from the street, and the rule says three ornaments, no more. Thin the flock a bit and I won't have to write it up for the committee.

rosa.thought_process: I'm at the Rec Center and nobody's around. Hal's confirmed for Saturday, and I invited him in person. I still need Donna and Gary locked in, and Donna is a pickleball person, so the Rec Center is probably where I'll find her. The afternoon shower may be keeping people off the courts. The ladder standings board could show who plays here and when, and might give me a note or contact to reach Donna. I shouldn't re-invite anyone I've already asked. Checking the board is a low-cost way to get a lead on Donna's schedule.

parameters.content: Check the standings and sign-up times to see when Donna usually plays

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
